Why Simcenter Micred T3STER?
Simcenter Micred T3STER is an advanced non-destructive transient thermal tester for the thermal characterization of packaged semiconductor devices (diodes, BJTs, power MOSFETs, IGBTs, power LEDs) and multi-die devices. It measures the true thermal transient response more efficiently than steady-state methods. Measurements are to ±0.01° C with up to 1-microsecond time resolution. Structure functions post-process the response into a plot that shows the thermal resistance and capacitance of package features along the heat flow path. Simcenter Micred T3STER is an ideal pre- and post-stress failure detection tool. The measurements can be exported for thermal model calibration, underpinning the accuracy of the thermal design effort.
Enable faster results with just one test
Simcenter Micred T3STER is easy to use and fast. It produces fully reproducible results, so each test only needs to be carried out once. Simcenter Micred T3STER tests packaged ICs using only electrical connections for powering and sensing, giving fast, repeatable results and eliminating the need for multiple tests on the same part. Components can be tested in situ and test results can be used as a compact thermal model or to calibrate a detailed model. 
Test all type of packaged semiconductors
Practically all types of packaged semiconductors can be tested, from power diodes and transistors to large and highly complex digital ICs, including parts that are mounted on a board, and even packaged into a product.
Simply put, a power pulse is injected into the component and its temperature response is recorded very accurately against time. The semiconductor itself is used both to power the part and to sense the temperature response using a temperature-sensitive parameter on the die surface such as a transistor or diode structure.
Access reliable software
The software provided with Simcenter Micred T3STER provides a lot of the value of the solution. That’s because the Simcenter Micred T3STER software can take the temperature versus time trace and convert it into what is known as a structure function. Discrete features of the package, such as the die attach can be detected in this plot, making Simcenter Micred T3STER an excellent diagnostic tool in product development. The plot can also be used to calibrate a detailed 3D thermal model in Simcenter Flotherm, creating a thermal model of a chip package that predicts temperature in both space and time with 99+% accuracy.
Achieve higher accuracy in electronics cooling simulation with measurement and calibration
This whitepaper considers factors for higher accuracy for modeling trace and connection heat dissipation within simulation. It illustrates thermal measurement of an IGBT module using Simcenter T3STER and model calibration in conjunction with thermal simulation in Simcenter Flotherm.

Simcenter T3STER capabilities
Thermal testing
The family of thermal characterization hardware solutions provides component and systems suppliers with the ability to accurately and efficiently test, measure, and thermally characterize semiconductor integrated circuit packages, single and arrayed LEDs, stacked and multi-die packages, power electronics modules, thermal interface material (TIM) properties, and complete electronic systems.
Our hardware solutions directly measure the actual heating or cooling curves of packaged semiconductor devices continuously and in real-time, rather than artificially composing this from the results of several individual tests. Measuring the true thermal transient response in this way is far more efficient and accurate, leading to more accurate thermal metrics than steady-state methods. Measurements only need to be performed once per sample, rather than repeated and an average taken as with steady-state methods.

What is thermal testing?
Thermal testing is the process of measuring and characterizing how heat moves through a component, package or system, and how that heat affects performance over time. For electronics, this means understanding junction temperature, heat flow paths and thermal resistance under real operating conditions.
Traditional approaches, such as thermocouples, infrared imaging or x-ray inspection, only tell part of the story. They capture surface temperatures or geometric detail but they can't reveal what's happening inside a component and some risk damaging the device under test in the process.

JEDEC-compliant thermal metrics 
Simcenter Micred T3STER uses an electrical test method compliant with JEDEC 51, delivering junction temperature accuracy within 1/100th of a degree. A single test generates the values that matter most — RthJC, RthJP and RthJA — ready to drop straight into your technical specification sheet.
One-click structure functions 
The test method uses the device itself as a temperature sensor, applying a power step and measuring the transient response. With one click, it converts that response into thermal impedance profiles and structure functions — fast enough for high-volume testing or production-line integration, even on complex designs.

Frequently asked questions
Why should I use Simcenter thermal testing solutions instead of alternative approaches? 
Unlike thermocouples, infrared imaging, or x-ray inspection, Simcenter Micred solutions use a nondestructive, JEDEC 51-compliant electrical method that reveals the complete internal thermal structure — not just surface temperature or geometry — with one-click results. Test data also connects directly to Simcenter Flotherm and Simcenter FLOEFD, enabling automated model calibration to over 99 percent accuracy. The result: customers report up to 78 percent time and cost reduction designing ECUs and a 30 percent increase in heat dissipation capacity and lifetime for power electronics modules.
Why is nondestructive thermal testing important?
Traditional methods like x-ray or invasive probing can damage the device under test or destroy it entirely, limiting how much you can learn. Nondestructive testing lets you evaluate the same component repeatedly, track degradation over its lifetime, and reuse test samples — saving cost while producing more reliable, repeatable data. 
What is JEDEC 51, and why does it matter?
JEDEC 51 is an industry-standard electrical test method for measuring thermal resistance and junction temperature in semiconductor devices. Compliance ensures your thermal metrics are measured consistently and are comparable across manufacturers, making it easier to specify components, validate datasheets, and meet customer or industry qualification requirements. 
What is a structure function, and what does it tell me?
A structure function converts a thermal transient measurement into a visual profile of thermal resistance versus thermal capacitance, layer by layer, from junction to ambient. It reveals the internal heat flow path of a component, making it possible to pinpoint exactly where degradation, imperfections, or design weaknesses exist. 
How is thermal testing different from thermal simulation?
Simulation predicts thermal behavior using computational models, while testing measures actual thermal performance on real hardware. The two work best together: test data validates and calibrates simulation models, improving their accuracy, while simulation lets you explore design alternatives quickly without building a physical prototype for every option. 
Can thermal testing handle new materials like SiC and GaN?
Yes. Simcenter Micred solutions support a wide range of semiconductor types and materials, including silicon-carbide (SiC) MOSFETs and gallium-nitride (GaN) HEMTs, in addition to traditional diodes, MOSFETs, IGBTs, and digital ICs — helping manufacturers characterize next-generation, high-power-density designs with confidence. 
What is active power cycling, and why is it used?
Active power cycling repeatedly stresses a component through switching and temperature transients to simulate real-world operating conditions over an accelerated timeframe. Combined with thermal degradation monitoring, it verifies predicted lifetime, isolates failure mechanisms, and identifies which design interfaces need improvement — without waiting for components to fail unexpectedly. 
Can thermal testing be integrated into production lines?
Yes. Automated, high-throughput thermal testing can be integrated directly into manufacturing lines for end-of-line (EoL) quality assurance. It verifies thermal performance on every unit, sorts output into quality bins, and supports standard communication protocols — helping manufacturers catch defects before products reach customers. 
When should thermal testing be incorporated into the manufacturing process?
Thermal testing delivers the most value when it spans the entire product lifecycle, not just a single checkpoint. Use it early in design to calibrate simulation models and predict lifetime, during pre-production to qualify reliability through active power cycling, and at end-of-line to catch manufacturing defects before products reach customers. Starting early and testing continuously — rather than only after a failure occurs — reduces redesign costs and helps ensure consistent quality at scale.
Can Simcenter thermal testing solutions be integrated with existing workflows and test environments?
Yes. Simcenter Micred hardware supports modular options — including boosters, cold plates, and controlled-environment chambers — to adapt to your existing test setup, and its software integrates directly with Simcenter Flotherm and FLOEFD for simulation correlation. On the production side, systems can be integrated with robotic handlers and support standard communication protocols like SECS/GEM, OPC UA, and Modbus, making it straightforward to fit into established manufacturing lines rather than requiring a separate, siloed process.
